title: Imaginary-ray convergence from derivative decay
statement: Let n∈ℕ, a∈ℝ with a>0, and H,G:ℂ→ℂ. Suppose G is continuous on {z∈ℂ : Im z>0}, and H has complex derivative G(z) at every point of that set. Suppose there exist real C≥0 and Y≥1 such that ‖G(it)‖≤C(1+t)^n exp(−at) for every real t≥Y. Then there exists A∈ℂ such that H(iy)→A as the real variable y→+∞.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : ℝ) (H G : ℂ → ℂ), 0 < a → ContinuousOn G {z : ℂ | 0 < z.im} → (∀ z : ℂ, 0 < z.im → HasDerivAt H (G z) z) → (∃ C Y : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ 1 ≤ Y ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, Y ≤ t → ‖G ((t : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ C * (1 + t) ^ n * Real.exp (-a * t)) → ∃ A : ℂ, Filter.Tendsto (fun y : ℝ => H ((y : ℂ) * Complex.I)) Filter.atTop (nhds A)
